question: Is a real Google Calendar selection run required before merging the final HTTP-normalization behavior, or will maintainers explicitly override the external-PR proof gate?
rationale: The patch is source-correct, but repository policy requires external PRs to show after-fix behavior in a real setup; the visible evidence is hermetic, mock-backed, and predates the final behavior commits.

options.title: Require current-head live proof
options.body: Ask for redacted output from a real Calendar event showing HTTP normalization, invalid-link skipping, event selection, and successful runtime URL normalization on e098f7bc.

options.title: Override the proof gate
options.body: A maintainer may explicitly accept the source, regression tests, and focused CI without a live Google account run.

recommendation.title: Require current-head live proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted output from a real Calendar event showing HTTP normalization, invalid-link skipping, event selection, and successful runtime URL normalization on e098f7bc.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the current assignee and authored the final behavior changes that postdate the contributor's proof.
